hook: If you wrung out a wet cloth in space, the water would not drip.
title: Wring a Washcloth in Space, No Drip
description:
Astronaut Chris Hadfield showed this on camera aboard the ISS. Wring a wet washcloth in microgravity and the water wraps around the cloth and his hands instead of falling. Surface tension holds it there. Part of our If You Were in Space series.

#Shorts #Space #ISS
comment_prompt: Would you try it? Yes or no

scenes.narration: If you wrung a wet cloth in space, nothing would drip.
scenes.headline: Wring It. No Drip.

scenes.narration: Astronaut Chris Hadfield showed this on camera.
scenes.headline: Chris Hadfield

scenes.narration: He squeezed the cloth with both hands.
scenes.headline: Squeeze Hard

scenes.narration: The water wrapped around it like a skin.
scenes.headline: A Skin Of Water

scenes.narration: It clung to the cloth and his hands.
scenes.headline: Clings To Hands

scenes.narration: There is no gravity to pull it down.
scenes.headline: No Gravity

scenes.narration: Surface tension holds the water in place.
scenes.headline: Surface Tension

scenes.narration: So in space, a wrung cloth stays wet.
scenes.headline: Still Wet
